content.title: Kara Lawson Stops Her Interview to Hold Duke Players Accountable
content.text: (Cory Knowlton-Imagn Images)Duke women’s basketball head coach Kara Lawson has built a reputation for demanding excellence, and that intensity was on full display during the Blue Devils’ recent NCAA Tournament preparations. In a viral moment that has captured the attention of the sports world, Lawson abruptly halted a mid-court media interview to address a standard-of-play issue she spotted during her team’s practice session.The exchange occurred as Lawson noticed a lack of focus and noise on the floor behind her. The former WNBA champion and Olympic gold medalist paused her response to hold her players accountable.Advertisement"Hold on, hold on," Lawson said, turning away from the microphones to deliver a sharp correction to her team. The clip, shared by sports anchor Kevin John, was captioned with a sentiment many fans echoed: "Duke head Coach Kara Lawson don't play!"Under head coach Kara Lawson, the Duke Blue Devils have cemented their status as a defensive juggernaut, culminating in a historic 2025-26 campaign. As per GoDuke, she was named the 2025-26 ACC Coach of the Year. Lawson has guided the program to a 27–8 record and its first ACC Regular Season Championship in 13 years.AdvertisementShe became the second-fastest coach in ACC history to reach 100 career wins, achieving the milestone in just 143 games. Her elite defensive schemes have the Blue Devils ranked 2nd nationally in blocks (6.4 per game) and among the top 15 in 3-point defense, stifling opponents throughout a dominant 16–2 conference run.After a challenging 3–6 start to the season, under her coaching, Duke ignited a 24–2 stretch led by sophomore sensation and All-American Toby Fournier, who leads the team in scoring (17.4 PPG) and rebounding. The momentum reached a fever pitch in the Sweet 16 on March 27, when senior guard Ashlon Jackson buried a buzzer-beating three-pointer to secure an 87–85 win over LSU. Now ranked No. 8 in the AP Poll, Duke moves on to face top-seeded UCLA, marking the program’s most successful era in over a decade.For Lawson, the cameras and reporters are secondary to the performance on the hardwood. By stopping the interview to enforce her standards, she sent a clear message to her roster: every rep matters, regardless of who is watching.AdvertisementThis story was originally published by Athlon Sports on Mar 28, 2026, where it first appeared in the College Basketball section.
